Outlines you draw are squared more readily: a house or bed whose corners are a little out, even one with a short wall drawn at a slant, comes out with square corners and its opposite sides parallel. Walls that line up, like the two sides of a T, end up on one line. Walls drawn at a clear angle, like a bay window’s, stay as you drew them while the rest is squared.

Moving a corner while you edit an outline’s points, it holds where its corners are square and its sides parallel to the others, with a small square mark in each square corner. Keep moving past it to put the corner anywhere else. Turning off squaring in Settings turns this off too.

On a phone, a corner you press while editing an outline’s points shows its angle and its two sides’ lengths well above your finger from the moment you press it, or beside your finger near the top of the screen, so they’re never under it and don’t jump when you start to drag.

A notice about something new now takes the place of an older one still showing: placing a plant that’s too close, too cold or needs a partner to fruit says so even while “Nudged… Undo” or another earlier notice is up. A plant’s own notices still come in order, crowding first. After you nudge a plant apart or move it, the next plant placed close to another is pointed out too.

Nudge apart moves a plant away from every plant it’s too close to at once: three placed in a triangle, the third moves out from between the other two. When the way straight out is blocked by its bed’s edge or another plant, it tries the other ways, the least move first, and only says there’s no room when none works. The notice names them all: “Nudged one Snowberry 2.3 ft away from the other two.”
